messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: sudden KV cache growth on quantized inference path for rwd/* models. Paging on-call @sam. Severity: P1-ish — customer latency and OOM risk. http://metrics.redwood/alerts/1769456789

alex (eng-runtime): seeing per-worker kv_cache_size_mb spike from ~800 -> ~2400 in the last 12m, correlates with an uptick in continuous-batching on quantized variants (int8/awq). GC not keeping up.

maria (eng-ml): quick note: AWQ/int8 path changes last night changed kernel selection fallback; we observed larger per-token KV footprint in profiling. likely layout change + alignment padding.

sam (oncall): acknowledged, I'll start triage. Can someone paste the top logs (worker memory + batch size) and the deploy that rolled yesterday?

alex (eng-runtime): paste logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T17:03:12Z worker-42 INFO kv_cache.size_mb=832 batches=18 avg_batch_tokens=320
2026-03-15T17:08:45Z worker-42 WARN kv_cache.size_mb=1286 batches=35 avg_batch_tokens=520
2026-03-15T17:15:01Z worker-42 ERROR kv_cache.size_mb=2456 batches=72 avg_batch_tokens=896 evict_fail=true
```
Deploy: rwd/runtime-release-2026-03-14 (includes quantization awq fallback kernels).

maria (eng-ml): confirming: the awq kernels allocate denser KV entries for keys (4 vs 2 words) for alignment on some GPUs, so int8/gptq/awq variants blow up cache footprint under heavy batching.

jen (eng-sre): immediate mitigation suggestion: 1) disable continuous-batching for quantized models, 2) reduce max_batch_tokens for those routes, 3) route critical customers to non-quantized variant. We should canary changes to a small pool first.

alex (eng-runtime): I can push a runtime hotfix to the hosted pool to flip per-model flags. Proposed hotfix (canary first):
```
# runtime flags
--model-route:rwd/qa-v2-quant.continuous_batching=false
--model-route:rwd/qa-v2-quant.max_batch_tokens=1024
--runtime.kv_compact_on_alloc=true
```
I'll target canary cohort (5% traffic) to verify memory stabilizes.

sam (oncall): do it. Also open a pager note for customer-facing CS. @customer-success-bot can you flag any 5xx/latency tickets from top customers (last 30m)?

customer-success-bot: Potential impact detected: AcmeAnalytics (org-acme) reporting errors in inference pipeline since 17:06Z. 5xx count increased from 2/min -> 45/min. Ticket created: CS-7894.

alex (eng-runtime): rolling canary patch now to pool-canary-3. Command: `./deploy-hotfix --canary pool-canary-3 --flags-file /tmp/kv-hotfix.json`

ops-runbook: runbook step 2 reminder: if kv_compact doesn't reduce footprint within 10m, revert to v0 non-quantized model variant or set model-route to fallback_variant=baseline.

(monitoring) 17:28Z alex: canary memory trend: worker avg kv_cache_size_mb dropped from 2200 -> 980 within 6m after compact + batch cap. No evict_fail logs now. Latency for canary traffic stable.

maria (eng-ml): nice. That confirms footprint was layout-related. We'll need a follow-up: rework AWQ packing and kernel selection heuristics to prefer compact layout for heavy-batched workloads.

jen (eng-sre): I'm going to start rolling the hotfix to prod with staged batches: 5% -> 25% -> 100% if no regressions. Watch for increased P99 due to smaller batches causing CPU pressure.

sam (oncall): rolling now. Also creating a temporary route rule for AcmeAnalytics: route to rwd/qa-v2-baseline (non-quant) for next 2 hours. Notifying CS. Command used: `./route-shift --org org-acme --to rwd/qa-v2-baseline --ttl 7200`

customer-success-bot: Notified AcmeAnalytics CSM. Patch ETA approx 15m, mitigation route applied.

(17:39Z) alex: prod stage 25% applied, memory trending down cluster-wide. Observed slight increase in tokens/sec but within SLO.

maria (eng-ml): note for postmortem: AWQ/int8 -> kernel selector picks kernel K4 on A100 which pads KV entries to 64-byte strides. Under normal traffic it's fine, but continuous batching multiplies the per-token state. We need a kernel-selection change to prefer compact-kernel K2 for high-batch scenarios on quantized models.

jen (eng-sre): agreed. Action items:
- CRITICAL: backport runtime hotfix to Dedicated fleet config (alex)
- ACTION: eng-ml to land kernel-selection guard (maria)
- ACTION: add metric alert for kv_cache_growth_rate (jen)
- CS follow-up with AcmeAnalytics and postmortem (sam)

sam (oncall): handing off to jen for next shift since I'm on call rotation ending in 25m. Key notes for handoff:
- Current status: hotfix fully rolled, cluster memory stabilized, Acme routed to baseline for 2h, CS ticket open (CS-7894).
- Watch: kv_cache_size_mb / worker, evict_fail logs, P99 tail for non-quant routes.
- Outstanding: eng-ml kernel patch PR #452 needs review; dedicated fleet patch pending.

jen (eng-sre): taking over. I'll keep channel live and ping oncall if the evict_fail resumes. Also will file incident tracking: INC-2026-0315-KV-QUANT and link CS-7894.

alex (eng-runtime): created commit and rollout plan for Dedicated fleet, targeting downtime window 02:00Z if agreed. PR: runtime#987.

maria (eng-ml): drafting kernel-selection change, will include microbenchmarks. PR: ml-kernels#452.

jen (eng-sre): good. Closing paging loop for now. Will run 1h of elevated monitoring then start postmortem doc. If anything spikes, re-open and page @sam. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT update: status=mitigated, mitigation=runtime hotfix + routing for affected orgs, start_time=1769456789, mitigated_time=1769457123

(THREAD END)
